chunks: Sahl, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Abdul Hameed, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When they frightened the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), the she-camel said to him: By Allah, I did not cease moving one hoof from the other, and even if I were cut into pieces, piece by piece.

key_terms.خُفّاً عَنْ خُفٍّ: one hoof from the other (steadfast movement)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet's camel say when it was frightened during the Hijrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the concept of *al-Insaniyyah* (personhood) in Shia theology, attributing speech and conscious endurance to the Prophet's camel during the Hijrah. The camel’s vow to keep its hooves moving even if severed underscores the unique spiritual status of the Prophet's belongings, serving as a metaphor for steadfastness in the face of adversity.

en.hubeali: H 14626 – Sahl, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Abdul Hameed, from the one whom he mentioned, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws said:

‘When they frightened the she-camel of the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>, the she-camel said to him<sup>saww</sup>; ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I will not move one foot from the other even if they cut me into pieces and pieces’.
en.sarwar: 178. Sahl, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Abdul Hameed, from the one whom he mentioned, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said:

‘When they frightened the she-camel of the Rasool Allah (saww), the she-camel said to him (saww); ‘By Allah (azwj), I will not move one foot from the other even if they cut me into pieces and pieces’.
